caption:
Bleach (2001): Tite Kubo is really good at dressing characters.

In one illustration, five characters wear the same white school shirt and gray trousers, but no two characters look the same. One collar is open, another tie hangs loose, the sleeves are rolled differently, the shoes change and one foot is bare. A few small choices are enough.

The other illustrations let him do more. Ichigo moves between goggles, headphones and oversized jackets. Renji gets louder colors and fur. Rukia wears small caps and fitted jackets, while Uryu gets long coats, gloves and heavy scarves. Orihime gets lighter dresses and wide hats. Across the set there is denim, plaid, baggy trousers, chocolate hearts and all-white summer clothes. There is a lot going on, but you can still tell everyone apart.

That is why the fashion in Bleach works. Kubo knows when one strong item is enough and when the whole outfit needs to change. Nothing complicated. Just very good clothes, drawn very well.

Seventy-four volumes. A lot of great outfits.

Bleach, 2001–2016 — Tite Kubo
